text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- State of Brandenburg orders first evacuations from floods as risk grows that dykes may burst.
- Dollar and DAX share index both climb further.
- Financial situation of state pension funds continues to deteriorate, report for 1997 shows.
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt blocks merger of Germany's Kali und Salz, a unit of BASG AG, and Canada's Potash Corporation of Saskatchewan.
- Public sector trade unions want to bring forward wage negotiations for 1998.
HANDELSBLATT
- Merger speculation among German banking stocks drives share market higher.
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel underscores demand that Germany's contributions to the European Union must be reduced.
- Former SS officer Erich Priebke convicted in Italy for role in 1944 Ardeatine Caves massacre.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl promises state aid for areas in eastern Germany hit by floods.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Members of public health insurance funds unlikely to face higher payments this year.
- Opposition Social Democrats join calls for reduction in German contributions to the EU.
- Hermann Otto Solms, parliamentary leader of Free Democrats (FDP), criticises plans to reform German spelling and grammar rules.
- Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp questions the sense of having a deficit criterion of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product for membership of Europe's single currency.
DIE WELT
- German security sources concerned about possibility of revenge attacks on Western leaders by Bosnian Serbs angered at NATO-led stabilisation force pursuing alleged war criminals.
- Germany and Austria want to play key role in negotiations over EU enlargement, their foreign ministers say.
- Kohl praises praises merger of west and east German rail systems as one of country's great success stories.
